No conflicts found.

The Proposed Change's Target File table (task-review-precheck.sh, validate-review-context-set.sh, and their .ps1 peers, plus an explicitly-unchanged check-workflow-state.sh) omits the file that actually constructs the reservation manifest validate-review-context-set.sh validates. That script's own usage line is 'manifest=$1' -- it consumes a manifest, it does not build one. I traced manifest construction to plugins/sdd-review-loop/skills/task-review-loop/SKILL.md STEP 2 and STEP 4, which instruct the orchestrating agent to assemble a 'Hash-verified allowed-input manifest including design.md, traceability.md, and plugins/sdd-review-loop/references/reviewer-calibration.md ... with current hashes' -- generic prose with no reference to precheck-result.json's tasks_sha256 or the new tasks_sha256_form field. No script under plugins/sdd-review-loop or plugins/sdd-quality-loop builds allowed_input_manifest programmatically (I searched for *manifest*/*reserve* scripts and found none that do this construction). The same SKILL.md demonstrates the author knows how to instruct copying a precheck-computed value when intended ('For full-profile features, copy the precheck's exact design_sha256, traceability_sha256, and four-entry layer_sha256 map into the top-level contract', SKILL.md:189-190) -- and tasks_sha256 is conspicuously absent from that list. validate-review-context-set.sh's own round-consistency comment ('A manifest freezes hashes at reservation time; the round's precheck-result.json froze them when the round opened. If the two disagree...') only makes sense if the manifest is computed independently of precheck-result.json, not copied from it -- corroborating the gap. Consequence: if task-review-precheck.sh is changed to record a normalized tasks_sha256 for mixed plans but task-review-loop/SKILL.md still instructs computing a fresh 'current hash' for the tasks.md manifest entry, the manifest will keep declaring the raw hash; validate-review-context-set.sh's form-aware comparison will then mismatch it, and every mid-flight task-stage reservation will fail closed -- the opposite of the stated Expected Effect. This is not a Category misclassification (the plugins/ carve-out is correctly satisfied here); it is an incomplete Target File list for a WFI that is otherwise correctly scoped, so the Expected Effect cannot realistically be achieved by modifying only the three currently-listed files.

The flowchart correctly routes to plugin-improvement, not measurement.

Problem Evidence is summarizable in 2-3 generic sentences (task-stage bindings on status-mixed plans break on every subsequent lifecycle transition because the producing side only emits raw-byte digests; this forced three unnecessary task decomposition review gate re-runs across three features in one session). Expected Effect states a quantitative target ('Average task-stage attempts per feature falls from 4.3 to 1.0'). No empty or vague issue-body risk.

Meta-Change: true is declared; all three sub-questions tested adversarially rather than accepted. (1) Does the change make a gate easier to satisfy without improving the underlying outcome? NO -- the normalized digest excludes only Status:/Approval:/Task-Review-Status:/Second Approval: fields, exactly the fields forms 1 (normalized_hash), 3, and 4 (rereview_normalized_hash) already elide today for any uniform-status plan; the raw form's incidental sensitivity to these fields on mixed plans is, per the WFI's own Root Cause Hypothesis, 'accidental in practice' rather than a designed defense, and task content (descriptions, dependencies, sizing, AC mapping -- what task-review actually judges) remains fully bound under the normalized form in every case. Tested circumvention of the tasks_sha256_form cross-check directly: precheck-result.json is itself a manifest entry subject to the unmodified, unconditional raw-hash-equality check for every path other than tasks.md, so its tasks_sha256_form field cannot be forged or substituted without independently failing that check; re-reading validate-review-context-set.sh's Change Description row ('every other manifest entry keeps the current strict raw-digest requirement') confirms it targets the generic per-entry raw-hash-equality loop itself, correctly scoped by path and by the verified form field, not merely the separate round-consistency check. (2) Non-decreasing guard: WFI states 'The change removes no gate, check or test. It adds one conditional on the producing side, one cross-check in the validator that does not exist today ..., and the five tests below, ... The count of deterministic checks strictly increases' -- verified consistent with the Proposed Change table and Verification Plan items 1-4. (3) Target-Metric independence: the Verification Metric (task-stage rebinds attributable to a status transition) is counted externally via task-review attempt-N artifact directories and commit history, not computed or self-reported by the modified scripts' own pass/fail logic -- it does not grade its own homework. All three sub-answers pass on independent testing.

proposed_revisions.change: Add a fourth row to the Target File table: `plugins/sdd-review-loop/skills/task-review-loop/SKILL.md` (STEP 2 and STEP 4 manifest-construction instructions, and the .ps1-equivalent orchestration path if one exists) -- 'When constructing the reviewer's hash-verified allowed-input manifest entry for tasks.md, first read the round's precheck-result.json. If it declares tasks_sha256_form: normalized, use that file's tasks_sha256 value verbatim as the manifest entry's declared hash instead of computing a fresh hash of the live file. Otherwise (form raw or absent) compute the current raw hash of tasks.md as today.' Also audit whether any other reviewer-launch skill (spec-review-loop, impl-review-loop) independently reserves a task-stage manifest entry for tasks.md and needs the same instruction.
proposed_revisions.rationale: validate-review-context-set.sh only validates a manifest supplied as its first argument; it does not build one, and no script in the repository constructs allowed_input_manifest programmatically. The manifest is assembled by the orchestrating agent per task-review-loop/SKILL.md's 'with current hashes' instruction, which today means a fresh raw sha256 of tasks.md and has no awareness of tasks_sha256_form. Without this revision, task-review-precheck.sh will start recording a normalized tasks_sha256 for mixed plans while the manifest keeps declaring the raw hash, so validate-review-context-set.sh's form-aware comparison will mismatch and every mid-flight task-stage reservation will fail closed -- the fix would not achieve its stated Expected Effect.
